acceptance_criteria: Every fleet JSON, SSE, proxy, and top-level error response is produced by one closed, versioned response-error projection.
Unknown exceptions and non-Error throws map to registered safe codes without returning message, stack, cause, command, stderr, location, environment, or arbitrary fields.
Typed validation errors expose only explicitly registered client-safe messages; Error identity and statusCode alone never authorize prose disclosure.
Filesystem, database, service-manager, and child-process failures map to bounded operation, stage, retryability, and failure-code vocabularies.
Mutation responses distinguish not-started, applied, rolled-back, rollback-failed, and unknown or inconclusive outcomes.
Internal diagnostics correlate to responses with bounded identifiers and classifications without making raw exception content part of the response contract.
Console consumers parse the versioned projection and render safe impact and next-action text without interpolating a raw response body.
Exact-byte negative tests inject reserved markers into Error messages, causes, paths, commands, stderr, and non-Error throws and prove absence from JSON, SSE, proxy, and console surfaces.
A static guard rejects direct errorMessage(err), err.message, arbitrary detail, or raw proxy-body response construction outside the approved projection.
blast_radius: Authenticated fleet JSON and SSE responses, proxied error adapters, route-local validation and mutation failures, console API error parsing and operator-visible rendering, filesystem and log-source diagnostics, service and child-process operations, rollback truth, and internal response-to-diagnostic correlation. No live fleet response, service, process, queue, message, credential, configuration, or production filesystem surface was inspected or mutated.

falsifier_or_remaining_gap: A pinned-main response projection would falsify this record only if every fleet JSON, SSE, proxy, and top-level error path used a closed versioned schema, arbitrary exception and filesystem markers were absent from response bytes, mutation and rollback state remained exact, and console consumers rejected raw or unknown responses. The inspected source disproved those conditions. This bounded audit did not launch a fleet server, invoke a real service manager or child process, or execute the wider route and console suites; real HTTP and SSE bytes, proxy compatibility, correlation behavior, static-guard coverage, every mutation-state branch, and client migration remain implementation verification obligations.
impact: Authenticated callers can receive upstream exception prose, absolute locations, operation details, command or service context, stderr fragments, and other version-dependent content that escapes into console UI, screenshots, browser telemetry, and support artifacts. Prose-shaped responses also prevent reliable retry, rollback, and mutation-state decisions and couple the public response contract to every upstream exception producer.
lead_verification_obligations: Re-read the live issue identity, body hash, labels, timestamp, exact SSH main, and every overlapping pull-request head and file page immediately before integration or metadata mutation.
Preserve #2178 and PR #2232 non-Error normalization and existing status behavior behind the new safe classifier rather than restoring unchecked casts or flattening operational truth.

Coordinate private correlation logging with #2164, the shared bounded failure vocabulary with #2447, log-source availability with #2513, and public health projection with #2515 without making those adjacent lanes hidden implementation owners.

Approve the versioned response fields, safe validation-message allowlist, operation and stage vocabulary, retryability rules, mutation-state and rollback-state semantics, and unknown-version behavior before implementation.

Require RED and GREEN exact-byte tests with reserved synthetic markers in Error messages, causes, non-Error throws, locations, commands, stderr, proxy bodies, and arbitrary detail across JSON, SSE, and console transports.
Verify not-started, applied, rolled-back, rollback-failed, and unknown or inconclusive mutation outcomes independently; a safe classifier must not turn ambiguous writes into generic failures.
Verify console clients parse only the approved projection, reject unknown versions and fields, and never construct or render an exception from an arbitrary response body.
Run the static response-construction guard against every fleet route and adapter and require an explicit reviewed allowlist for any client-safe prose.
Re-read privacy-withheld pull-request refs by pull-request number in a non-public surface before integration.
Keep live fleet responses, services, processes, queues, messages, credentials, configuration, production filesystems, and rollout outside the draft implementation pull request.

suggested_remediation: Introduce one fleet response-error module with a closed versioned projection for code, operation, stage, retryable, mutation_state, rollback_state, and correlation_id. Map unknown, filesystem, database, service-manager, child-process, proxy, and validation failures through explicit safe classifiers; keep raw diagnostics behind the private logging boundary. Migrate route-local JSON and SSE catches, the generic wrapper, proxy adapters, and top-level catcher without losing status or mutation truth. Change the console API to parse the projection and render registered impact and next-action text rather than arbitrary response bytes. Add reserved-marker exact-byte tests and a static construction guard, then coordinate shared vocabulary and availability semantics without merging this independently reviewable response boundary into logger or health ownership.
